claims.label: Host Says Multiple Influencers Used Identical "Overwhelming" Language
claims.claim: The host says the collage she displays shows multiple influencers using the word "overwhelming" to describe the evidence against Tyler Robinson at the preliminary hearing.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference timestamps and language across influencer posts to determine whether messaging was coordinated.

claims.label: Josh Hammer Calls the Hearing Evidence the Most Overwhelming He Has Seen in His Life
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, Josh Hammer says the evidence presented during the pre-trial evidentiary hearings in the trial of Tyler Robinson is "the most overwhelming presentation that I have ever seen this early on during a legal proceeding in my entire life."
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Hammer's stated impression against the actual hearing exhibits.

claims.label: Host Plays Pre-Hearing Clips Asserting Tyler's Parents Turned Him In
claims.claim: In clips the host plays, multiple media figures from before the hearing assert that Tyler Robinson's parents identified him from news footage, questioned him about his grandfather's gun, and helped him turn himself in to authorities.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare pre-hearing narrative claims against actual preliminary hearing testimony transcripts.

claims.label: Lance Twiggs identified Tyler Robinson only by generic clothing items
claims.claim: In a hearing clip the host plays, Lance Twiggs testifies that he would not say with 100% certainty because of camera quality, but that the person looks like Robinson in terms of the shoes, the sunglasses, the jeans and, though he had not specifically seen him in that hat, he was usually wearing a hat.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference Lance's testimony with other witness identifications and the exhibits discussed.

claims.label: Host Says Lance Twiggs Confirmed Tyler Robinson Was Not Political
claims.claim: The host says Lance Twiggs confirmed her report that Tyler Robinson was not political; in the hearing clip she plays, Twiggs testifies that Robinson talked about politics more than he did, usually things he heard on the radio on the drive to work, and that he had never heard Robinson talk about Charlie Kirk specifically.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Lance's testimony against text messages introduced as A-2123.1.

claims.label: Miss Noble reported seeing a bald man with three others driving the gray Challenger
claims.claim: The host says the woman who captured the Ring camera footage, Miss Noble, told police she saw a bald man driving the gray Challenger accompanied by three other people; in the hearing clip the host plays, the witness answers, "I believe they thought that was the case."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Ring camera footage and police interview transcripts for cross-verification.

claims.label: Host Says Court-Displayed Car Had Dual Exhaust; Tyler Robinson's Actual Car Had Single Exhaust
claims.claim: The host says the Dodge Challenger shown in preliminary hearing footage had dual exhaust pipes, while Tyler Robinson's actual Dodge Challenger had a singular exhaust system.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain vehicle registration and VIN data for Tyler Robinson's Challenger to verify exhaust configuration.

claims.label: Exhibit 12.4 does not show Tyler Robinson taking the shot
claims.claim: Witness testimony confirmed that Exhibit 12.4 compilation video shows movements believed to be Robinson on campus but does not include footage of the alleged shooting itself.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify whether any other exhibit purports to show the shooting itself.

claims.label: Witness in Hearing Clip Says Exhibit 12.1 Differs from 12.4 Only by Red Circles, Face Blurring, and Zoom
claims.claim: In a hearing clip the host plays, a witness testifies that Exhibit 12.1 differs from Exhibit 12.4 only by (1) red circles/ovals highlighting individuals, (2) face blurring of parking garage bystanders, and (3) zoom in/out on the rooftop segment.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain certified copies of both exhibits for direct comparison.

claims.label: Host Says Leaked 12.1 Footage Shows Only a Pixel Running Across Rooftop
claims.claim: The host says Court TV accidentally captured footage of the 12.1 enhanced exhibit, which she says is the same video as 12.4 zoomed in; in a clip she plays from an X user, the speaker says that at 1h17m30s of Court TV's Day 2 the figure running across the rooftop is only a pixel.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full Court TV Day 2 footage for independent analysis.

claims.label: Caitlyn Oliver testified media "DNA on the gun" framing was scientifically indefensible
claims.claim: ATF forensic biologist Caitlyn Oliver testified that characterizing media reports as "Mr. Robinson's DNA is found on this item" would constitute a "source attribution" that is "not scientifically defensible."
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Caitlyn Oliver's testimony against ATF report language and media headlines for accuracy of characterization.

claims.label: DNA samples from trigger/trigger guard were mixed samples with at least 4–7 contributors
claims.claim: Caitlyn Oliver testified that DNA samples from the trigger and trigger guard were mixed samples with at least 4–7 contributors, with "major" and "minor" labels referring only to DNA quantity contributed, not to any activity-based attribution.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the full DNA report to verify contributor counts and threshold interpretations.

claims.label: Host Says Tyler Robinson's DNA on the Gun Was the Most Degraded of All Contributors
claims.claim: The host says that Caitlyn Oliver confirmed, in testimony the host plays, that Tyler Robinson's DNA sample was the most degraded of all contributors found on the firearm (swab 1.3 of trigger/trigger guard).
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference degradation findings with handling/timeline assumptions in the prosecution's theory.

claims.label: 6A bullet jacket fragment diameter measured 286–301 thousandths of an inch
claims.claim: ATF ballistics expert Samantha Carner testified that the 6A bullet jacket fragment had a diameter range of 286 to 301 thousandths of an inch.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference measured diameter with .30-06 SAAMI specifications and the recovered rifle.

claims.label: Benny Johnson claimed the court showed 4K HD video of Robinson committing the murder
claims.claim: Benny Johnson claimed in his post-court video that the court displayed "high-definition quality video 4K of Tyler Robinson committing the murder of Charlie Kirk" on "giant screens" with "crystal clear" visibility of face and license plate.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Johnson's claim against Court TV leaked footage (A-2122.1) and witness testimony on 12.1 enhancements.

claims.label: Ben Shapiro's security received live updates during Charlie's transport
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, Ben Shapiro says his security was on the phone with Charlie's security while Charlie was still in the back of the car, and they were getting updates along the way; the host describes the ride to the hospital as approximately 7 minutes.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the person in Charlie's vehicle who provided the updates; verify against witness accounts of Brian Harpole, Rick Cutler, Frank Turek, Dan Flood, and Justin Davis.

claims.label: Host Displays Tyler-Lance Text Messages Including Specific Phrases
claims.claim: Per text messages between Tyler Robinson and Lance Twiggs that the host displays on-screen, the messages included lines such as "I am stuck in Orem for a little while longer yet," "if I'm able to grab my rifle unseen," and "Some hate just can't be negotiated out."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain certified chat exports and metadata; cross-reference with the disclosed Tel Aviv extraction vendor (see N-10713).

claims.label: Host says Tim Pool and Jeremy Boreing lied about who received live updates from the transport car
claims.claim: The host says Tim Pool is lying through his teeth, that he did not receive updates from somebody in that car about Charlie Kirk's status, and that Jeremy Boreing lied when he tried to pretend that her own security was getting those updates; she says she confirmed her security was not on the phone with anybody in that car.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify who in the car was in contact with outside security teams and when.
claims.transcript_snippet: Tim Pool is lying through his teeth. He did not receive updates from somebody in that car about Charlie's status.

claims.label: Host offers a $10,000 bounty for evidence of who Ben Shapiro was at lunch with in LA when Charlie Kirk was shot
claims.claim: After asking who on Ben Shapiro's security team was receiving updates on Charlie Kirk's condition, the host asks who he (caption: "Bench Crew") was at lunch with in LA when the shooting happened, says she has a hunch, and offers a $10,000 bounty for evidence, sent to the tip line.
claims.investigative_direction: Collect tip-line submissions on the lunch; corroborate any named attendee against location data or witnesses.
claims.transcript_snippet: I will put up $10,000 bounty on that piece of information.

claims.label: Host says Bill Ackman immediately pledged $1 million to Tyler Robinson's father, Matt Robinson
claims.claim: Recapping the pre-hearing narrative that Tyler Robinson's parents turned him in, the host says Bill Ackman ("Bill Ackman" in the captions) immediately pledged $1 million to Tyler Robinson's father, Matt Robinson, for "the brave act" of turning in his son, and says someone should check on that $1 million.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate Bill Ackman's original pledge post and any record of payment to Matt Robinson.
claims.transcript_snippet: In fact, Bill Ackman, King of the Hamptons, immediately pledged $1 million to Tyler Robinson's father, Matt Robinson.
claims.uncertainty_note: Host account; the pledge itself is not shown. Matt Robinson has no person node (person band full, awaiting Daveed).

claims.label: Host Says Erika Invited Influencers to the Courthouse but Not to the Private Funeral Mass
claims.claim: The host says Erika Kirk extended an invitation to influencers including Benny Johnson, Graham Allen and Brandon Tatum to come to the courthouse, although she did not invite them to Charlie Kirk's private funeral mass.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the hearing attendance and seating list and any invitation messages from Erika Kirk's office to the named influencers.
claims.transcript_snippet: did not choose to invite to Charlie's private funeral mass, but extended an invitation for them to come to the courthouse.

claims.label: Host Says Benny Johnson Announced That Erika Asked Him to Be at the Hearing
claims.claim: The host says Benny Johnson said at the outset that Erika Kirk asked him to be at the preliminary hearing.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate Benny Johnson's original post or video stating that Erika Kirk asked him to attend.
claims.transcript_snippet: Benny Johnson came right out of the gate and said, "Erika asked me to be here."

claims.label: Commentator Cites Three Confessions by Robinson
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, an unnamed commentator says there are three confessions by Tyler Robinson: one to his parents, one to his roommate and one on Discord.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the commentator and compare each claimed confession against what was actually entered into evidence at the hearing.
claims.transcript_snippet: So, we have three confessions here. one to his parents, one to his roommate, and one on Discord.

claims.label: Host Recaps Narrative That Robinson Acted in Rage Over Trans Rights
claims.claim: The host recaps the pre-hearing narrative that Tyler Robinson killed Charlie Kirk in broad daylight in a burning rage over LGBTQ and trans rights, because he has a trans furry boyfriend named Lance Twiggs.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the motive narrative against the indictment, the charging documents and Lance Twiggs's hearing testimony on politics.
claims.transcript_snippet: in a burning rage over LGBTQ rights, particularly trans rights because he has a trans furry boyfriend named Lance Twiggs.

claims.label: Host Recalls Promise That Footage of the Shot Would Be Released Later
claims.claim: The host says that before the hearing the public was constantly reminded that there was footage of Tyler Robinson taking the shot, and that it had simply not been presented to the public yet.
claims.investigative_direction: Collect the official statements promising footage of the shot and check whether any such footage was entered as an exhibit.
claims.transcript_snippet: we were constantly reminded uh that there was going to be footage also of Tyler Robinson taking that shot, that it had simply not been presented to the public yet

claims.label: Host Says Erika Told Viewers She Had Seen the Evidence and Was Convinced
claims.claim: The host says Erika Kirk told viewers back in November or December that she had seen the evidence and was convinced it was Tyler Robinson, and that by her interview with Bari Weiss her mind was made up.
claims.investigative_direction: Review the Erika Kirk interview with Bari Weiss and any earlier Erika Kirk statements about having seen evidence.
claims.transcript_snippet: Erika herself told us back in November or December that she had seen the evidence and she was convinced it was Tyler Robinson.

claims.label: Host Says Narrative Presented Robinson's Prints and DNA on the Gun Exclusively
claims.claim: The host says the public was told Tyler Robinson's fingerprints and DNA were found on the gun, that this was presented rather exclusively, and that other prints were never mentioned.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare earlier official and media statements about prints and DNA with the ATF laboratory reports.
claims.transcript_snippet: Now, we were also told that Tyler's fingerprints and his DNA were found on the gun and that was presented rather exclusively.

claims.label: Host Says Parents Did Not Turn Robinson In
claims.claim: The host says she maintained that Tyler Robinson's parents did not turn him in, and calls the parents-turned-him-in story a mainstreamed lie.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the Washington County Sheriff's Office arrest narrative and search warrant records on how and with whom Robinson arrived.
claims.transcript_snippet: I maintained that Tyler Robinson's parents did parents did not turn him in. Okay, that was a mainstreamed lie.

claims.label: Host Says Mike Mitchell Told the Robinsons They Could Do It the Easy Way or the Hard Way
claims.claim: The host says she maintained that Mike Mitchell, a former undercover detective, family friend and Tyler Robinson's boy scout leader, was the one told Robinson would be brought in, and that he told the parents to do it the easy way or the hard way, so Robinson agreed to come in willfully without confessing.
claims.investigative_direction: Interview Mike Mitchell or the Robinson family about the surrender; obtain police records of who contacted the family before Robinson went in.

claims.label: Host Says Robinson Was Not Political and Came From a Family of Trump Supporters
claims.claim: The host says she told viewers that Tyler Robinson was not political and came from a family of Trump supporters.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull voter registration and donation records for the Robinson household and compare with Lance Twiggs's testimony.
claims.transcript_snippet: Um, I also expressed to you that Tyler Robinson was not political, crucial, and that he came from a family of Trumpers.

claims.label: Host Says the Gun Was Robinson's but Was Not Fired That Day
claims.claim: The host says she has never denied the gun found was Tyler Robinson's, but asserts it was not fired that day and was not used to kill Charlie Kirk, and that he had inherited it as a family heirloom as the firstborn son.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain ATF test-fire and bullet comparison reports and the chain of custody for the rifle.
claims.transcript_snippet: I have never denied that the gun found was indeed Tyler Robinson's gun, but rather I have asserted that the gun was not fired on that day and was not used to kill Charlie Kirk.

claims.transcript_snippet: but that Tyler himself was actually more of a fisherman. His brothers were the hunters.

claims.label: Host Says Lance Twiggs Is a Federal Asset Who Gathered Tyler's Belongings and Is Blackmailed
claims.claim: The host says she has suggested from the beginning that Lance Twiggs is a federal asset who gathered Tyler's belongings to pin the crime on him, and that she suspects Lance is heavily blackmailed because he was into some dark web stuff.
claims.investigative_direction: Look for court filings or records on any agreement with Lance Twiggs and on the alleged dark web activity; no document has been shown on air.

claims.label: Host Says Lance Twiggs Got Immunity and Was Not Cross-Examined Despite Hearsay Objections
claims.claim: The host says every piece of evidence the influencers push relies on Lance Twiggs, who she says was immediately granted immunity by the feds and was not allowed to be cross-examined at this hearing even though arguments were made that his testimony amounted to hearsay.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the immunity or cooperation agreement and the hearing transcript rulings on hearsay and cross-examination of Lance Twiggs.

claims.label: Host Says Feds Flooded the Zone With Brunette Decoys She Calls Maroon Boys
claims.claim: The host says she suggested the feds intentionally flooded the zone with multiple brunette young men in similar outfits, whom she termed the maroon boys or decoys, and that she showed footage of many such men on campus.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the host's published decoy footage with campus video entered at the hearing to count distinct individuals in similar clothing.

claims.claim: The host says her biggest claim was that Tyler Robinson did not step foot onto campus that day, which is what he told his family, namely that he was around campus but not physically on it.
claims.investigative_direction: Establish Robinson's movements through campus access logs, parking records and phone location data.
